Life Dashboard / Grafana stack
Open sourceNo cloudNo account

A self-hosted Grafana dashboard for your health data

The Life Dashboard stack is an open-source Docker Compose setup for both apps: a receiver that checks signatures, Postgres and six Grafana dashboards. It's for people who want their records in SQL rather than in Home Assistant.

Run with Docker Compose

Demo data

What it does

Six dashboards

Overview, Activity, Sleep, Heart and body, Screen time, and Data and sync, provisioned in a Life Dashboard folder.

Try it without a phone

The demo profile posts 60 days of made-up data for two phones through the real receiver.

Every record in Postgres

One records table with a JSONB column holds all 33 Android types and 28 iPhone types without schema changes.

SQL views for your own queries

The dash schema turns raw records into days, nights, hours and apps in your time zone.

A receiver that checks signatures

It verifies the X-Signature HMAC, applies a repeated payload once, and removes the records the phone reports as deleted.

Android and iPhone side by side

Each phone gets its own label in the webhook URL and shows up as its own Phone in every dashboard.

Dashboards

Sleep, activity, heart and screen time in Grafana

Every dashboard has a Phone picker and links to the other five that keep the time range. Each panel has an info icon that says where its figure comes from.

  • Life Dashboard overview How today and last night went, and this week against the four before it.
  • Activity and Sleep Steps by hour, workout minutes against the WHO guideline of 150, a hypnogram, bedtime and wake time.
  • Heart and body Heart rate per hour, resting heart rate, HRV, SpO2, breathing rate and weight with its 7-day mean.
  • Screen time, Data and sync Minutes per app and per day, the last use before sleep, and when each phone last sent data.
All six dashboards
How it counts

No scores, and a gap where data is missing

Nothing is colored as good or bad. Goals are dashed lines you can change at the top of a dashboard.

  • Steps counted once Steps, distance and calories come from the phone's daily totals, so a walk recorded by phone and watch counts once.
  • Local days in your time zone A night belongs to the morning you wake up. Today is marked “so far” and left out of averages.
  • HRV kept apart RMSSD from an Android watch and SDNN from an Apple Watch are different measures, so they're never mixed.
  • Gaps, not zeros A missing day shows as a gap. The only red is a phone that sent nothing for 24 hours.
Postgres and SQL

Your health data in Postgres, ready for your own queries

The dash views hold one row per day, night, hour or app, with local days already worked out. Query them with psql or in a Grafana panel of your own.

  • dash.activity_days Steps per day, counted once, per phone.
  • dash.sleep_nights Hours asleep, deep and REM per night.
  • dash.screen_apps Minutes per app per day.
  • A read-only Grafana user grafana_ro can only read the records and views, and its queries stop after 30 seconds.
Every view, column and unit
Install

Run the stack

Life Dashboard stack

Postgres and Grafana dashboards, self-hosted

Run with Docker Compose

Clone the repository, set four values in .env, then docker compose up -d --build.

  • Demo data Available60 days of made-up data for two phones, before any phone of yours is involved.

What you need

Docker with Compose, on a machine your phone can reach on the same network or over a VPN. On each phone, Life Dashboard Companion for Android or for iPhone, pointed at the receiver's webhook URL on port 8080 with a label for that phone, and the same secret as WEBHOOK_SECRET. To reach the receiver from outside, put a reverse proxy with TLS in front of it. The stack is offered as a starting point you can change, not as a finished product. Set a WEBHOOK_SECRET: without one the receiver accepts unsigned payloads.

Receives from Life Dashboard Companion for Android and for iPhone.

Try it with demo data
git clone https://github.com/owen282000/life-dashboard-stack
cd life-dashboard-stack
RECEIVER_PORT=18080 GRAFANA_PORT=13000 \
  docker compose -p lifedash-demo \
  --profile demo up -d --build

Give it a minute, then open http://localhost:13000 and log in as admin with the demo password lifedash. For your own data: cp .env.example .env, set four values, then docker compose up -d --build; the quick start has the details.

FAQ

Questions about the stack

Can I try it before I connect a phone?

Yes, if you can run Docker. The demo profile starts the stack with 60 days of made-up data for two phones, under its own name and ports. The commands are under Run the stack. Without Docker, the screenshots on this page show the same dashboards.

Can I put it on the internet?

Put a reverse proxy with TLS in front of the receiver only, and allow request bodies of 32 MB. Keep Grafana on your own network or behind a VPN: anyone who can view a dashboard can read every health record through the data source. On your own network, change GRAFANA_PASSWORD and GRAFANA_DB_PASSWORD in .env before the first start: Grafana's admin password defaults to lifedash, and both Grafana and the receiver listen on every interface of the machine. The Postgres owner's password is fixed in docker-compose.yml; Postgres publishes no port, so only the receiver reaches it.

Can I use it next to Home Assistant?

Yes, as a second home for the data, with two things to know today. The app keeps one signing secret per tab, and pairing with Home Assistant sets it, so a stack with its own secret then refuses the payloads: run the stack without a secret or with the same one, or send one phone to each. And a payload counts as delivered once one destination takes it, so if the stack is down at that moment, it misses that payload.

How do I back it up?

One pg_dump line writes a dump, and one pg_restore line puts it into a fresh stack. Restart the receiver afterward so it rebuilds the views and the grafana_ro grants.

Can I change the dashboards?

Yes. They're provisioned from grafana/dashboards/life-dashboard/, so Grafana won't save changes over them: use Save as for a copy, or edit the JSON file. Keep views of your own in the public schema, because the receiver rebuilds dash at every start.

What doesn't it do yet?

Series sent per time window are stored, but only the heart rate panels read them, so leave Data Resolution on Every record. Days follow the stack's one time zone, and a backfill doesn't remove records the phone no longer has. The known gaps list the rest.

I already run Grafana. Can I use mine?

Yes. Run the receiver and Postgres from the stack, and in your own Grafana add a PostgreSQL data source for the stack's database with the read-only user grafana_ro and your GRAFANA_DB_PASSWORD. Then import the six dashboard files from grafana/dashboards/life-dashboard/ and pick that data source. grafana_ro can read the records, the buckets and the dash views, and nothing else.

Life Dashboard

Life Dashboard is an open-source project by Owen Vogelaar, in four parts: the Life Dashboard Companion apps for Android and iPhone, a Home Assistant integration and a Grafana stack. It isn't related to other apps or templates called Life Dashboard. Questions go to Discussions.

This site sets no cookies, runs no analytics and loads nothing from anyone else. Site privacy.
